questions.design_consequence: Pin entrypoint plus construction history, not “W128” alone
questions.unresolved_item: historical binary/process snapshot unavailable.
questions.answer_summary: `best_agents(seats=range(4), worlds=128, seed=0) -> dict` loads one Python model/table then separate SearchAgent/Searcher/native Env/Mlp per seat. Tail `dd_left=6` means `13-floor(n_played/4)<=6`, including an incomplete current trick. Bid search is enabled. Effective best seed is `seed+2*seat`: factory adds seat, SearchAgent adds it again. Explicit `search:` specifications default to `w=32,dd=0,show=0` and their seed path differs. Live `tuppi_ai_search_v1` constructs best agents; deal evaluation `--checkpoint best` does too, but ignores a separately supplied equity file for candidate construction. Replay/review has distinct budgets/configuration initialisation; review defaults W256/confirmation1024 and resets sooli settings on evaluation. It is not a literal live policy replay. A second live entrypoint, `tools/serve_human.py`, replaces the server constructor with a seat-plan wrapper: default `1:incumbent,2:search,3:incumbent`, W128 unless TUPPI_AI_WORLDS overrides, v3 rules and review enabled. It retains old profile labels, so a displayed incumbent label does not identify its actual seat policy. This differs from the native server profile selecting best for all requested seats. Actual running process environment and virtual-environment import resolution were not inspected; E062 documents the v3 environment pointing to ENGINE. Command templates require that environment, not an arbitrary system Python.

questions.status: ESTABLISHED-IN-CODE / UNKNOWN for historical runtime state
questions.design_consequence: PolicyFork and lifecycle ledger prerequisite to exact comparisons
questions.unresolved_item: no supported complete snapshot/restore API.
questions.answer_summary: Searcher retains NumPy RNG, mutable ctypes uint64 RNG and native environment. Native slots retain RNG and deal state; setting/cloning a deal does not copy/reset RNG or sooli configuration. `reset_all` starts matches using current RNG, not cold construction. Python globals in evaluation hold policies throughout worker tasks. Each best seat has its own mutable search environment, but process-global rollout chunk and thread-local solver caches persist. Model inference has no recurrent state; `last_values` is diagnostics, not an explicit memory of blind intent. Solvers use thread-local tables; absence of deadlines makes cache contents intended to affect work rather than exact values, contingent on solver correctness, which was not re-probed.

questions.design_consequence: Use full typed observations; neural vectors are insufficient information keys
questions.unresolved_item: own hidden-commit memory is not in the engine observation.
questions.answer_summary: PlayerObservation includes actor/observer/team/partner, dealer/forehand, phase, ordered own hand and legal actions, shows/public shown cards, contract/declarer/leader, completed/current tricks, team trick totals, score/terminal flags, ruleset/schema/visibility and protocol refs. V3 adds `bids_locked`; sooli adds decisions, soolaaja, exchange flag, given/returned cards and three-player trick history. Nonacting seats have empty legal-action tuples. Blind observations hide all committed declarations, including one's own, until resolution; `bids_locked` gives count, not cards. The live UI's remembered submitted bid is a different information channel from this policy interface.

questions.design_consequence: Name the exact sampler version and approximation; do not call it all legal information
questions.unresolved_item: fallback constraints absent natively; sooli rejection truncation.
questions.answer_summary: Ordinary native sampling fixes own cards, unplayed public shown owners, played-card removal, proven voids and each seat's capacity. Capacity uses actual per-seat play counts, so an incomplete trick is asymmetric. Suit count allocations are weighted by combinatorial completion counts using floating log arithmetic, then cards shuffled/split. The intended base law is uniform over these constraints, drawn pseudorandomly with replacement; layouts can repeat. SplitMix/modulo and floating arithmetic are not a proof of exact rational uniformity. No importance weights are returned.

questions.answer_summary: For acting team t, the native value is `sign(t)*float32(V0(next_score,next_dealer)-V0(source_score,dealer))`, accumulated in float64 and averaged over W. V0 is a fitted match-win surrogate in [0,1], so Y is an equity change in [-1,1], not tricks or probability of winning this deal. Subtracting the common starting value cancels in action gaps. Terminal V0 is1/0. Table rows:0 for0–0,1..12 for Team0 scores4..48,13..24 for Team1 scores4..48; column1 means Team0 deals, column0 Team1 deals. `Equity.load` recomputes values from the stored DealModel, not from a trusted frozen table blob.

questions.design_consequence: Use the tested contested-round oracle as a layout proxy
questions.unresolved_item: no exact deployed-law analytical mean.
questions.answer_summary: Canonical `suits.play_out(own_ranks,opponent_ranks,*,times_led,policy)->tuple[int,...]` sorts hands and makes each nonempty holder play its lowest/highest rank each abstract round, recording winners. `conditional_layouts(...seen_ranks,hand_sizes,void)` yields three rank-tuples and exact Fraction weights based on filler-card capacity combinatorics. The compact agent copy's `expected_ducking_tricks` uses contested rounds only. Its brute-force equality test walks rank index i and counts a root win only if some other hand has an ith card. The exactness is combinatorial under fixed simplified play, not a theorem about optimal Tuppi strategy. `card_liability` is kept expected tricks minus shed expected tricks; a discarded card is removed, not reassigned to opponents.

questions.design_consequence: Factor native initial-world loop; retain its continuation loop

questions.answer_summary: The call graph is SearchAgent→Searcher.action_values→native.search_values→search_core→sample_world_sooli→forced actions→sooli/DD/MLP→signed mean. Per-world variant shares this path. Proposed `research_evaluate_worlds(env:Env,mlp:Mlp,obs:TcObs,worlds:Sequence[TcDeal],actions:int32[K],tail:int,streams:StreamPlan)->ActionWorldBatch` must not sample, reconfigure, reload, or substitute tails. questions.design_consequence: Explicit independent stream namespaces; preserve comparator call schedule
questions.unresolved_item: batching invariance not newly tested.
questions.answer_summary: One shared RNG produces layouts; sooli continuations get a base draw mixed with world/action slot index. Same worlds therefore do not imply identical continuation randomness. Changing K/action order changes streams. Ordinary NOLO continuation has deterministic clone/DD and no sooli, so evaluating the reference once on each fixed world and reusing it preserves its conditional distribution. Do not generalise that to bids. Proposed stream namespaces `fit`, `cheap`, `expensive`, `reference`, `validation` derive independently from recorded experiment seeds, with fitting deals disjoint. The frozen comparator runs its original RNG allocation; candidate instrumentation must not consume its stream. Chunk32→128 is reported move-preserving, not revalidated here; regrouping worlds/actions can change more than throughput.

questions.design_consequence: Monte Carlo mean under exact chosen law, not imported closed form
questions.unresolved_item: strengthen constraints only as a separate candidate.
questions.answer_summary: Old conditioning knows own ranks, gone cards, capacities and suit voids, but not multiple shown-card ownership, cross-suit constraints or fallback implications. Native sampling has the former ownership constraints but lacks fallback exclusions. Per-world liability is still defined for every supplied layout. At a mid-trick discard, remove all already played cards, then remove candidate from root hand; start fresh abstract within-suit rounds over the remaining unequal hands. This deliberately does not resolve the partial current trick. Because root is void in its led suit, it cannot win that trick; future cross-suit lead effects remain a proxy limitation.

questions.design_consequence: Define commitment versus reached-call estimands separately
questions.unresolved_item: native reconstruction is not behavioural conditioning.
questions.answer_summary: Live humans commit without seeing prior bids; the runner resolves them in order, requesting AI bids only while reached. Engine/native collection is sequential computationally. At seat k, having been called means earlier actual bids were NOLO, although their cards are hidden in the observation. Native sampler reconstructs earlier NOLO cards from hypothetical hands using random legal choices. It is solving a reached decision approximation with a hand law that did not condition on actual predecessor pass policies. Later unused human commitments have no direct rules effect.

questions.design_consequence: Side-effect-isolated policy forks are required
questions.unresolved_item: querying all four is not behaviourally neutral.
questions.answer_summary: Four clone bids can be obtained from separate own masked precommit observations under common complete layouts. Four actual search calls consume RNG, can initialise/update sooli settings, and affect later play. Even when an unused commitment has no rules effect, evaluating it can have computational effects. Current best has no explicit remembered-bid feature, but its random/configuration history persists. Thus `Q(a)-Q(b)=E[1(E)*(Ua-Ub)]` is valid for a fixed simultaneous-policy model with action-independent unused-call state; it is not established for the literal current call-suppression process. Document either a faithful fork/call schedule or a separately identified model experiment; do not silently clean up the live baseline.

questions.design_consequence: Distinguish surrogate equity from score and match wins
questions.unresolved_item: equity artifact's exact generation sample not recorded.
questions.answer_summary: At0–0 winner receives points; when already up, same team's win adds points, other team's win resets to0–0. Terminal is score≥52; overshoot is legal. Nonterminal completed deals rotate dealer. Current equity solves a50-state approximation (25scores × dealer parity), using one dealer-win probability and conditional point distributions for all scores. The artifact's dealer-win probability is.49575. Fitter source defaults20000 incumbent self-play deals at0–0 with rotating dealer; a default is not proof of the file's sample size/seed. Legacy `match_transition_value` is signed score/52 with terminal±1, not this table. Do not transplant it into C1/C2/C5.

questions.unresolved_item: no practical finite reduction established for full persistent state.
questions.answer_summary: Score/dealer omit sooli settings, RNG/call history and restoration/construction context. Independent-randomness idealisation removes literal PRNG bits only if state transitions and policy marginal laws are stationary; it does not remove the v3 configuration defect. A possible augmentation includes each seat's relevant sooli mode, policy identity and option state, but reachable-state and transition sufficiency still need proof. Complete literal machine state is finite in principle, not a practical100-state method. Cold-resetting every row would define a different instrument and may be useful only with a new identity.

The current equity's parity reduction is its modelling assumption, not an established symmetry for every proposed pairing.

questions.answer_summary: Ordinary DD computes exact team trick totals with alpha-beta/cache, not score-equivalence bounds. At48, margin does not affect the winning team's next score utility, but winner identity still matters. With history-dependent future policies, equal next scores alone do not establish equal actual match value.

That is competent rollout modelling, not a claim it equals actual searching players. Search continuations need nested sampling/RNG-state integration and cannot be substituted silently. Fixed partner policy is also fixed; C5 does not optimise it cooperatively.

questions.design_consequence: Add weighted-history groups and persistent root option
questions.unresolved_item: no existing expected-value contingent-plan store.
questions.answer_summary: Proposed `WeightedHistory{world_state,weight,seat_policy_states,root_memory}` and `InfoGroup{root_key,histories,legal_actions}`. For each root action advance frozen other seats; group by complete later root observation; evaluate one common b for each group using normalised conditional weights and accumulate group mass times best conditional utility. Deterministic observed other actions give likelihood0/1; stochastic policies require likelihood factors. Do not reset to hard-uniform belief on the next real root turn. Store the chosen option's mapping and posterior or re-solve from exactly that posterior through deal end.

questions.status: PARTIAL / costs UNKNOWN for new objective
questions.design_consequence: Gate on public information and full-support completion, enforce caps
questions.unresolved_item: 1680 is a count ceiling, not a runtime proof.
questions.answer_summary: Existing NOLO code meters transitions and returns budget statuses; N11 reports cost for its adversarial objective, not this expected-value option. At a three-card trick boundary9 unseen cards have at most1680 unconstrained allocations, but future observations/actions and policy cost still matter. Proposed gate: ordinary actual actor, exactly three remaining cards each at boundary, complete support under declared constraint model below a prespecified cap, compatible deterministic policies and reconstructible information. Mid-trick eligibility needs a separately justified bound. A monotonic node/time cap triggers unchanged W128 fallback, records reason and discards incomplete exact claims. Off-support observations or policy mismatches invalidate the option and fall back, with failures retained. The .5-second experience target is distinct from an old10-second ceiling; no cap chosen from favourable pilot outcomes.

questions.design_consequence: Compare complete options, not just first actions
questions.unresolved_item: W128 future-call state fork is prerequisite.
questions.answer_summary: Diagnostic1 values W128's selected root action followed by C5-optimised later root play. Comparator2 actually runs W128 at every later root decision against the same named other policies, with the correct lifecycle. Only2 represents its deployed continuation under that model. For an information-relaxation bound, reveal world only to root while holding other policies fixed. fixtures.construction: Construct a v3 explicit deal with seat k not forehand; collect earlier legal NOLO commitments through the engine. Export the focal observation before its bid. Verify empty visible show list, correct `bids_locked`,13 own cards, no predecessor hand/bid content, and at least two legal declarations/cards. Separately retain original four hands and actual commits. Pair with a hypothetical layout in which the named deterministic predecessor clone chooses RAMI; the focal observation must stay identical while evaluator-only E differs. Forehand companion control requires E=1. A reached-only fixture alone cannot validate unconditional event weighting.

Use a development explicit deal, four legal NOLO shows, then legal plays until actor is void in led suit with at least two cards in different suit-liability situations. Export completed/current trick order and all public shows; retain no other hands in legal record. Require unequal remaining capacities at this partial trick and, in one companion, two shown cards of the same suit. Enumerate small supplied layouts for the contested oracle; ensure at least one action gap/proxy varies across worlds. Root cannot win the current off-suit trick; do not claim the proxy models future lead allocation. E024's test is the exact within-suit oracle cross-check, not a fabricated full-deal fixture.

Start a v3 development explicit deal, resolve bids and legal sooli decisions, accept the frozen offer policy's choice, stop before give. Export soolaaja's13-card observation and13 exchange actions. Truth retains all original hands and offer selection facts. Require two legal gives with differing downstream transfer value; acceptance-conditioned population metadata is part of the case. A forced accept may be used for a unit test only and must not be labelled naturally accepted pilot data.

Branch F03 on a specified legal g, stop before return. Export partner's14-card own hand, legal13 returns excluding g, and legal `given_card`; returned_card remains unavailable. The giver's remaining12 cards are absent. Recover original P for receiver features by removing g from its14, not by consulting truth. Pair hidden layouts holding this full receiver information fixed; outputs must agree. Add a candidate convention in which informative g is expensive to transfer, so the survival test can reject a poor signal. After return validate13/13,39active/13dead and defender observations without g/r.

Replay a development ordinary NOLO or RAMI deal through ten complete tricks, stop at actual actor with three cards. Export root legal observation and full public history; keep possible layouts evaluator-private. Require complete support≥2, a non-forced current root choice and a later non-forced choice under at least one branch. Construct independent toy continuations where indistinguishable worlds prefer opposite later actions, and a companion where observable future events separate them. Verify enumeration count independently and reject key collisions. A two-card boundary companion is a control, not primary strategy-fusion evidence. Run v3 round-trip/ruleset preservation before accepting the fixture; current legacy reconstruction is not sufficient.

A pure rules-object fixture can use `MatchScore(48,0)` and validated `DealScore` objects for each winner at different legal margins. DERIVED structural expectations: Team0 win at any positive legal award reaches≥52 and V0=1; Team1 win resets to0–0 rather than awarding Team1 a fresh lead. For nonterminal continuation dealer rotates; terminal future dealer is not needed for V0. Repeat with teams swapped, zero-score awards and an overshoot. These are arithmetic expectations, not measured game outcomes. A rollout fixture additionally needs two feasible differing margins with the same winner and one branch where winner remains uncertain, to prevent unsafe stopping simply because score is48.
